.SYNOPSIS...18/749 PM.

It will rain tonight into Thursday morning. It will the potential
for flooding and wind related issues. Very large surf and high 
tides will continue, with ongoing surf and flooding hazards at the
coast. Cool and dry on Friday and Saturday. A chance of light rain
on Sunday.

&&

.SHORT TERM (WED-SAT)...18/843 PM.

***UPDATE***

The front is currently moving through the Central Coast. Rainfall
totals, so far, have not been overly impressive save for the NW
tip of SLO county where 1.5 to 3.0 inches of rain has already
fallen. The rest of the area has received a half inch or less.

The front will pass through southern SBA county and VTA county
overnight and then into and through LA county in the morning and
perhaps early afternoon.

While rain rates are not too impressive at the moment. All short
term mdls are showing a nice increase in rates as the front rounds
Pt Conception. Rainfall totals may come in a little less than
advertised.

The front has not been producing any thunder at all, but still a 
20 percent chc seems reasonable as some enhancement is beginning 
to show at the base of the front.

***From Previous Discussion***

During the peak periods of rain, rates will easily reach a half 
inch per hour, with areas of 0.75" per hour and localized areas 
of 1 inch per hour. These highest rates will most likely occur in 
the mountains, with the best chances in the Santa Barbara and 
western Ventura Mountains. Storm totals remain about the same, 1-2
inches most coast/valley areas, locally up to 3 inches in areas
with the highest rain rates, most notably parts of southern Santa
Barbara County. South facing slopes 2-5".

This storm is expected to be very convective when the strongest
part of the storm moves through so expect to see around 2-4 hours
of thunderstorms in most areas. Along with that, there is a very
small chance, 5% or less, of a weak tornado with the best chances
of that in the LA Basin on Thursday.

During the heaviest part of the storm wind gusts up to 35 mph are
possible at lower elevations and up to 50 mph in the mountains.
For this reason, it would be prudent to avoid parking vehicles 
under trees and being mindful of any heavy patio furniture. There 
is a flood watch in all areas except the Antelope Valley, so 
expect streets and freeways to be very wet and slick and at times 
un-passable.

Freezing levels will remain above 7500 feet for all but the last
few hours of the storm, during which 3-6 inches could fall mostly
above 7000 feet. Due to the very high elevation and limited
impacts no snow related products will be issued.

Dry weather will return Friday and Saturday with light offshore
flow and highs mostly in the 60s.

.LONG TERM (SUN-WED)...18/312 AM.

A little pop up ridge moves through the state on Saturday. It will
make it a dry day with sunny skies. Despite the ridge and sunshine
max temps will not change much and will remain 5 to 10 degrees blo
normal.

Mdls have sped up the next system. It is not very strong it will
likely bring rain to the Central Coast, but will only have about a
40 percent chc of bringing rain to areas south of Pt Conception.
Up to a quarter inch of rain may fall across the Central Coast. If
rain does make it south of Pt Conception, rainfall totals will not
exceed a tenth of an inch. Max temps will continue in the mid 60s.

Another pop up ridge will cross the area Monday. Dry and mostly
sunny conditions will prevail. Temps will not change much.

Not the best agreement within all of the various mdls but another
system seems possible later next Tuesday or Wednesday. There is a
20 percent chc that this could be a decent sized system.

&&

.AVIATION...19/0027Z.

At 2315Z at KLAX, there was no marine layer nor an inversion.

Overall, moderate confidence in 00Z TAF Package. A frontal 
system will move through the region bringing gusty south to 
west winds with -SHRA to RA. Confidence is lower on wind shift
and rain timing (+/- 2 hours). MVFR conditions are expected
with LIFR to IFR vsbys possible in heavier rains. Frontal
turbulence is possible. There is a 20% chance of thunderstorms 
through the period, starting this afternoon. 

KLAX...Moderate confidence in TAF. Worst conditions likely 
19/13-18Z as a strong line of storms is expected bringing
gusty/shifty winds LIFR-IFR vsbys possible, along with
a 20% chance of TSTM. There is a 40 percent chance of an 8-10 kt 
east wind component from 19/08Z-15Z.

KBUR...Moderate confidence in TAF. Timing of wind shift and
rain may be off +/- 2 hours. LIFR-IFR vsbys possible 13-18Z.
There is a 20 percent chc of a TSTM after 12Z.

&&

.MARINE...18/652 PM.

High confidence in dangerous ocean conditions through Friday due 
to a combination of gusty winds and large seas. Conditions have
deteriorated along the Central coast this evening indicated by
buoy observations gusting over 35 kts from the south and seas 
10-15 ft as of 6 PM. Gale force winds will still be possible 
elsewhere but will likely remain more localized. Also, light to 
moderate rain with pockets of heavy rainfall is being observed. 
This front will continue to progress to the southeast overnight 
into Thursday morning. A marine weather statement (MWSLOX) has 
been issued to highlight the potential for thunderstorms. Refer 
to the product for more information. Winds will shift to the NW 
behind the front and showers will likely linger into Friday.

Seas will continue to increase due to the combination of a large 
northwest swell and southwest wind swell. Large breaking waves may
impact Morro Bay Harbor and to a lesser extent Ventura Harbor 
from Wednesday through Thursday. Additionally, Pismo and Cayucos 
may see breaking waves at or over the base of the piers.

Conditions will improve through the day Friday and become relatively
mild through Saturday. A weak front will likely move through the
coastal waters Sunday into Monday but impacts look minimal at most.
Better signal for an impactful storm system around Thanksgiving 
but details are blurry at this time.

&&

.BEACHES...18/652 PM.

Dangerous conditions at the beaches will continue into Friday, 
peaking Thursday.

Large surf will create very dangerous rip currents and jetty
conditions. Additionally, minor to moderate coastal flooding 
issues may occur, especially on Thursday during peak morning 
high tide. Some impacts may be shallow seawater flooding over 
low lying beaches/walkways/parking lots and significant beach 
erosion. Impacts along the Central Coast will likely be higher 
such as localized wave damage (especially to piers, localized 
coastal flooding impacting roads and possibly structures, as 
well as breaking waves at Morro Bay Harbor.

High Surf Advisories have been issued for all beach areas. A 
Coastal Flood Advisory is in effect for the Central Coast for 
Thursday.

Extremely high tides, likely record breaking, will occur over
Thanksgiving week (peaking Tuesday through Thanksgiving Day). 
Additional swells are becoming increasingly likely next week as
well. These swells may produce period of elevated to high surf.
The combination of very high tides and increasing surf will likely
lead to at least widespread moderate-level coastal flooding 
issues across all coasts. There is potential for significant 
coastal flooding impacts if a larger swell overlaps with the
timing of the extreme tides
